courses.title: The Lost Generation Close Reading
courses.instructorBio: Elena studied Comparative Literature and Information Science at Columbia University. For the past two years, she has been leading literary discussion groups. This will be her ninth group, following deep dives into works like East of Eden, Anna Karenina, One Hundred Years of Solitude, The House of Mirth, The Great Gatsby, and The Brothers Karamazov.
courses.description: In this series, we'll use the writers of the Lost Generation (Hemingway, Fitzgerald, Stein) as a master class in close reading. You'll learn to slow down on the page, notice what the prose is doing beneath the surface, and build the kind of literary attention that transforms how you read any book.

courses.title: The Odyssey Close Reading
courses.instructorBio: Elena is the founder of Close Reading NYC, a literary community offering in-person reading groups and workshops in Manhattan. She holds a double major in Comparative Literature and Computer Science from Columbia University and has led close readings with Fractal for two years. She has guided readers through classics such as Moby-Dick, Middlemarch, The Brothers Karamazov, and Anna Karenina, among others.
courses.description: This course will explore the art of deep engagement through the practice of close reading. Using The Odyssey as our guide, we will move deliberately through key episodes of the epic, returning to specific passages, tracing patterns, and asking what Homer reveals about topics such as wandering, homecoming, desire, restraint, and recognition. Each session includes guided close reading, structured discussion, and selected supplementary materials to deepen our understanding of the poem's historical context, oral tradition, and enduring philosophical force.

courses.title: Writing as a Quick Bite: Intro to Flash Fiction
courses.instructorBio: Sara earned her MFA in poetry from the University of Houston. Her writing appears or is forthcoming in several literary journals including Indiana Review, Washington Square Review, Dialogist, trampset, and others (read more at sarakaplancunningham.com). Full time, she is a high school teacher in Bed Stuy, and has taught first year writing at the University of Houston, as well as creative writing.
courses.description: In this class, we'll be writing flash fiction. We will also be practicing how to see the world in a way that will carry over to your writing. In this class, you'll encounter: generative prompts, homework reading and writing assignments, discussions of writers' "strategies," and new uses for those scraps of conversation you hear on the subway.

courses.title: Improv Writing Lab
courses.instructorBio: Crystal Duan combines her background in fast-paced journalism (where she had to write 1,200+ words daily on deadline) with expertise in Jungian psychology to create a unique approach to writing unblocking. With bylines in the Washington Post, Minneapolis Star Tribune, and more, she understands both the craft and the psychology of effective writing. What sets Crystal's approach apart is her focus on the emotional and somatic aspects of writing - not just what you write, but how it feels to write it. Her coaching identifies specific patterns of self-criticism and helps you develop a more productive relationship with your creative self.
courses.description: Lab to help writers overcome writer's block and develop spontaneity and authenticity through timed writing exercises and coaching.

courses.title: Worldbuilding for Storytellers and Narrative Designers
courses.instructorBio: Sarah is an editor and publisher of award-winning speculative fiction. She studied history and literature at Stanford, and she thinks about worldbuilding through an interdisciplinary lens.
courses.description: This interdisciplinary seminar explores how fictional worlds operate as structured models of society, drawing on speculative fiction, history, anthropology, and political theory. Students analyze how environments, institutions, culture, memory, and technology shape social order, while building a single evolving fictional world across the semester. The course culminates in a cohesive "world dossier" integrating these elements into a fully realized speculative society that can be used as a platform for creative projects.

courses.title: Intuitive Movement
courses.instructorBio: Clara Wiest is a swiss artist, based in NY for almost 10 years. They are a stage, movement and intimacy director as well as a performance artist. Their whole life has been movement focused; They grew up going to circus school for 12 years, ballet, capoeira, contemporary and modern dance, they have extensive training in Feldenkrais, Alexander Technique, Clown and Mime, Lucid body, Qi Gong, somatic practices, Hypnotherapy and Energy Healing, as well as trauma-informed body work.
courses.description: Movement is a tool for us to feel more connected, aligned and alive. In this course you will be given the space and tools to start creating and/or deepening your relationship to your body. The goal of this course is that you leave feeling more in tune with yourself, find a sense of play, that you leave with tools to keep deepening in your relationship with yourself on your own.

courses.title: Parkour for Everyone
courses.instructorBio: Jianing Zhao is an interdisciplinary movement and theater artist with backgrounds in contact improv, contemporary dance, dabke, ballroom, Kpop, pole and aerial dance, hair hanging, martial arts, parkour, and freestyle skiing. Her movement practice explores the multiplicity and dynamism of connective points and dimensions between one's own body and other physical and sociocultural bodies and spaces. She has been practicing parkour since 2022 and sees it as a form of movement research that bridges physical exercise, creative exploration, and embodied engagement with public space.
courses.description: This course invites students of all backgrounds to explore efficient and expressive ways of moving through urban space that feel playful and accessible in their own bodies. Through guided individual and group exercises, we'll interact with everyday features like walls, railings, stairs, benches, and trees, and see familiar parts of this city in a fresh light.

courses.title: Butoh: Into the Depth
courses.instructorBio: I am the director of the New York Butoh Institute with 25 years of experience teaching and performing butoh. www.vangeline.com
courses.description: Learn to meditate through movement, tapping into subtle body systems and the unconscious. Butoh, the dance of darkness, is a transformative practice from Japan being taught in Brooklyn by renowned teacher Vangeline. Open to dancers and non-dancers alike.

courses.title: Applied Taijiquan
courses.instructorBio: I've been teaching self-defense community workshops with a wide range of students over the past 7 years, refining my ability to convey movement concepts to people of all skill levels. In my 20 years practicing martial arts, including Taijiquan, Baguazhang and Xingyiquan, my focus has been on developing all of the benefits Internal Martial Arts (IMAs) have to offer, from the meditative and therapeutic to the more active body skills.
courses.description: Delving into the concepts and practices needed to build practical skill in the martial art of Taijiquan, this class focuses on learning in layers to examine the form's nuanced meaning, and training ways to bridge that meaning into detailed body awareness, dynamic problem-solving, and powerful movement literacy.

courses.title: Dhamma Dance Club
courses.instructorBio: Michael is an avid facilitator of authentic relating, acucircles, and authentic movement containers, and is curious how they integrate into the moment-to-moment. Most nights in the week, you may see him at the club.
courses.dates: 6 weeks open RSVP, then 6 weeks closed cohort
courses.description: Attendees will deepen easeful concentration, sensory clarity, and equanimity and integrate them in social contexts. They will also build confidence to move authentically in and out of the club while exploring nightlife in NYC.

courses.title: The Hidden Power of Groove: Intro to Street Dance
courses.instructorBio: I'm a dancer, dance teacher and former software engineer with training in street & club dance styles including hip hop, house, vogue femme, waacking, kpop, choreography, and freestyle. Having started dance as an adult who often felt confused and overwhelmed in traditional beginner classes, I've become passionate about making movement more accessible, intuitive, and enjoyable for non-dancers. I currently teach beginner-focused dance classes and design learning experiences that help people grow confidence, expression, rhythm, and freedom through movement.
courses.description: Imagine hearing your favorite song come on and feeling excited to jump in instead of wondering what to do. Drawing from street dance styles born on dance floors and at parties (Hip Hop, House, Waacking, and Vogue), this structured beginner class teaches the foundational skills that make dance feel more natural, expressive, and fun. No pressure to "get it right." Just a clear path to building confidence in your body and discovering your own style. Whether you're an absolute beginner, a dancer exploring a new style, or someone simply looking to feel more at home in your body, this class is for you.

courses.title: Drum Circle 101
courses.instructorBio: Hi, my name is Christian and I have loved drumming for as long as I can remember! I have studied and performed in many different styles over the years, including symphonic percussion, marching band, drum set, West African, Afro Latin, Brazilian, and Celtic. Most recently I have had the opportunity to perform with Mambembe Brazilian drum group and The Empire Marching Elite marching band at parades, events, Brooklyn Cyclones games, and even at Radio City Music Hall! I believe that rhythm is something universally human, as natural as our heartbeat. Something that each of us has within us, ready to unlock and tap into. I enjoy teaching others the art of drumming, and I am looking forward to sharing my knowledge and experience with you.
courses.description: Do you want a deeper understanding of rhythm that makes singing, dancing, drumming, and even walking more fun, groovy, and natural? In this 7 week rhythmic journey we will explore drumming and percussion in ways that can be applied anywhere – your body, voice, the kitchen table, drums, shakers, pots and pans… your imagination is the limit!

courses.title: The Structure of Sound: Mathematics of Music
courses.instructorBio: Surya Raghavendran is a researcher in mathematical physics and a Gibbs Assistant Professor in the math department at Yale, with broad interests in how mathematics shapes the world around us. The mathematics of music is a favorite instance, and this course is his attempt to share it.
courses.description: Much of what you're taught about music looks arbitrary - twelve notes to an octave, some intervals consonant and others not, every instrument tuned slightly wrong - but almost none of it is. Over five weeks we work out the mathematics behind it, from how the ear hears a pure tone to the symmetry of the chromatic scale, picking up Fourier analysis, a little number theory, and some group theory on the way.

courses.title: Build a Poker AI Bot
courses.instructorBio: I'm finishing up my Economics PhD at Carnegie Mellon, and a Data Science/Modeling Intern at Revelio Labs. This class is based on the Poker AI Challenge at CMU, in which I participated.
courses.description: Over 6 weeks, we're going to build a bot to play a variant of poker. By the end, you'll have learned the underlying theory and have a functioning bot. After the class I'll test the bots against each other and give a prize to the top bots.

courses.title: Fractal Accelerator
courses.instructorBio: Andrew Rose, Founder of Fractal, Fractal University, and Fractal Bootcamp, has trained 100 engineers in the last two years following his career as a software engineer and educator. Liam Duffy is a senior software engineer at Seso Inc. with over a decade of engineering experience; he leads the adoption of AI engineering practices at Seso and brings that real-world expertise to Fractal Accelerator students.
courses.description: The inventors of computers imagined machines that could extend thought, creativity, and agency — "instruments whose music is ideas." That hasn't quite happened yet, but it's starting to. In this 6-week Saturday course, you'll learn to make your computer truly yours: building custom tools, automating busywork, connecting AI agents to your apps and data, and shipping real software starting from nothing but a plain-language description of what you want. No programming experience required. You'll leave with a personal AI agent that knows who you are, runs in the background, and keeps working when you walk away.

courses.title: Basics of Computational Biology
courses.instructorBio: I've been working in the bioinformatics field for about 9 years. I currently work at a biotech startup, and before that I worked in academia and completed a PhD in this field. I've also taught the class 6 times already and I think people have mostly enjoyed it.
courses.description: This course is a basic introduction to computational biology / bioinformatics, meant for programmers who already know a bit of Python. No prior biology knowledge required!

courses.title: Making a Lamp: 3D Modeling, 3D Printing & Design
courses.description: In 6 weeks, learn how to build a 3D model and design by making a lamp. No experience necessary, this will be an introductory course. We will discuss 3D modeling best practices for 3D printing, as well as making methods such as sewing and soldering.

courses.title: How to Make a Planter: 3D Modeling for 3D Printing
courses.description: Make your own 3D printed planter and become an emerging 3D modeler from no previous experience!

courses.title: Urban Gardening Practicum
courses.instructorBio: James Hunt has worked to develop and sell agtech software, helped create companies that store carbon in grasslands and forests, and moonlights as a guerrilla gardener around New York City.
courses.description: Learn from a regenerative agriculture expert how to think about space, soil, sprouting, and planting in the unique environment Brooklyn affords us. Every student will have the opportunity to start their own seeds from a wide selection and take home a customized mini urban garden for continued practice.

courses.title: Unconscious Mind Journey Group
courses.instructorBio: Christian's mission is to make the world a better place by helping people reach their true potential – people who feel good in their mind and body, make healthy decisions, form strong secure relationships, create positive change in their communities, and make their dreams reality. He specializes in breakthrough coaching with individuals and groups using cutting-edge symbolic and metaphorical landscape methods. Christian is credentialed with the International Coaching Federation, the Hypnosis Training Academy, Lumia Coaching, and the Wim Hof Method Academy.
courses.description: Join us for a journey into the unconscious mind, where limiting beliefs, identity, habits, and blocks live. In this 7 week course we will update your inner landscape to be healthy, supportive, positive, and optimized for you to live the life you want to live!

clubs.name: Controversial Politics Salon
clubs.description: Have you ever wished you could just be honest with your peers about your political thoughts, especially your uncertainties and confusions, without making it into an argument? Or wanted a community of curious people who were trying to make serious political progress, especially on ideas outside the overton window, instead of merely having the right opinions on all the popular issues?

clubs.name: The Last Summer Lecture Series
clubs.description: Suppose that this was the last time we could steer the world before radical change. Where should we go together? Should we imagine a world with AI from scratch, or build on the great conversation of history? Do we return to stories of old, or to ourselves, or each other? Xiq invites some of his favorite people to answer these questions.
clubs.schedule: Saturdays, time varies — join the WhatsApp for details

clubs.name: The Founding Debate Reading Group
clubs.description: In 2026, the United States turns 250. To mark the anniversary, we're reading the arguments the founders had with each other — particularly the Federalists and Anti-Federalists — about the system of government they were building. We'll spend eight weeks in primary sources and a little scholarship, trying to understand how they were thinking and what they were afraid of. 30–50 pages a week.

clubs.name: Claude Squad
clubs.description: Do you like burning calories and burning tokens? Wanna set PRs while merging PRs? Then join the Claude Squad at Vital Williamsburg every other Thursday as we prompt, lift, sauna, and dine together while aura farming and friendshipmogging everyone with our matching outfits! Make no mistake, we're the funnest fitness and computing cult in NYC 💪
clubs.schedule: 6:30 pm, usually every other Thursday. Join the WhatsApp group for dates.
